messages.subject: Re: summarize_all() and approx()
messages.body_plain:
Hi all

> I'm trying to get summarize_all() to work with approx(). More concrete,
> the data frame df is to be interpolated to height_target:
>
> library(tidyverse)
> df <- tibble(height = c(0, 10, 20),
>              a = c(1, 3, 5),
>              b = c(4, 6, 8))
> height_target <- c(5, 15)
>
> For the a column, the commands works like this:
>
> approx(x = df$height, y = df$a, xout = height_target)
>

> To apply it to all columns, I would do something like
>
> summarize_all(df,
>    funs(list(approx(x = height, y = ., xout = height_target)$y))
> )
>
> This, however, gives the error
>> Error in summarise_impl(.data, dots) :
>>  Evaluation error: 'x' and 'y' lengths differ.

In  a discussion on https://stackoverflow.com/q/45409032/1463740 , I
found the error: The problem is that the interpolation creates a new
column height first which is then used for the interpolation of the
other columns. Due to the different vector lengths, this cannot work.
Thus, height has to be identified directly:

df %>%
 summarise_all(funs(list(approx(x = df$height, y = ., xout =
height_target)$y))) %>%
 unnest()

Cheers
Sebastian

messages.subject: na.rm=TRUE not respected within summarize for some variables
messages.subject_clean: na.rm=TRUE not respected within summarize for some variables
messages.body_plain:
I have encountered a situation where na.rm=TRUE for mean() is not respected within summarize. The following example illustrates the issue using a portion of a larger data file. When I recreate the data file by hand there is no problem. Am I missing something here?
## testNARM.R
library(tidyverse)
library(rio)

origData <- import("https://www.dropbox.com/s/g2pw8eljoc8lh72/origData.RData?raw=1")

print(origData)

## na.rm respected.
print("Missing using Ct")
checkMissing <- origData %>%
  group_by(genotype, condition) %>%
  summarize(meanEf1a = mean(Ct, na.rm=TRUE),
            n=n()) %>%
  print()

## na.rm not respected.
print("Missing using ex")
checkMissing <- origData %>%
  group_by(genotype, condition) %>%
  summarize(meanEf1a = mean(ex, na.rm=TRUE),
            n=n()) %>%
  print()

## Re-create the data by hand.
byHandData <- tibble(sampleNumber=as.integer(c(33,34,35,36)),
                   genotype=factor(c("WT","WT","Casp1","Casp1"),
                     levels=c("WT","Casp1","Sluggish","control")),
                   condition=c(rep("none.PIC.18",4)),
                   gene=factor(c("Ef1a.2","Ef1a","Ef1a.2","Ef1a")),
                   Ct=c(NA, 7.420775, 7.685127, NA),
                   ex=c(NA, 1.0121389, 0.9831145, NA))
print(byHandData)

## na.rm respected.
print("Missing using Ct")
checkMissing <- byHandData %>%
  group_by(genotype, condition) %>%
  summarize(meanEf1a = mean(Ct, na.rm=TRUE),
            n=n()) %>%
  print()

## na.rm respected.
print("Missing using ex")
checkMissing <- byHandData %>%
  group_by(genotype, condition) %>%
  summarize(meanEf1a = mean(ex, na.rm=TRUE),
            n=n()) %>%
  print()

messages.subject: What would cause inner_join_impl to thins a 'character' is a 'list'
messages.subject_clean: What would cause inner_join_impl to thins a 'character' is a 'list'
messages.body_plain:
Comrades,

I seem to have cornered myself into a situation where I'm finding it
very difficult to put together a reproducible example.

I'm trying to inner_join two tables but inner_join_impl thinks
something (the join column(?)) is a 'list' instead of a "CHARSXP"

The issue is that there are no list columns in any of the two tables
I'm trying to inner_join.

Here is the code that is throwing an error:

R> xx = tx.info <http://tx.info> %>% inner_join(tchrom.info <http://tchrom.info>,
by=c("feature_id"="ensembl_transcript_id"))

And the error:

 Error in inner_join_impl(x, y, by$x, by$y, suffix$x, suffix$y,
check_na_matches(na_matches)) :
   Value of SET_STRING_ELT() must be a 'CHARSXP' not a 'list'

And some context for the two objects I'm trying to join

R> head(tx.info <http://tx.info>)
 # A tibble: 6 x 3
   feature_type         feature_id    name
          <chr>              <chr>   <chr>
 1       enstid ENSMUST00000070533  Xkr4_1
 2       enstid ENSMUST00000208660   Rp1_1
 3       enstid ENSMUST00000194992   Rp1_2
 4       enstid ENSMUST00000027032   Rp1_3
 5       enstid ENSMUST00000027035 Sox17_1
 6       enstid ENSMUST00000195555 Sox17_2

R> head(tchrom.info <http://tchrom.info>)
head(tchrom.info <http://tchrom.info>)
 # A tibble: 6 x 5
   ensembl_transcript_id chromosome_name start_position end_position strand
                   <chr>           <chr>          <int>        <int>  <int>
 1    ENSMUST00000000001               3      108107280    108146146     -1
 2    ENSMUST00000000003               X       77837901     77853623     -1
 3    ENSMUST00000000010              11       96271457     96276595      1
 4    ENSMUST00000000028              16       18780447     18811987     -1
 5    ENSMUST00000000033               7      142650766    142666816     -1
 6    ENSMUST00000000049              11      108343354    108414396      1

And sapply(tx.info <http://tx.info>, is.list) and sapply(tchrom.info <http://tchrom.info>, is.list) confirms
that there are no list columns in sight ...

I'm running:

 R version 3.4.0 (2017-04-21)
 Platform: x86_64-pc-linux-gnu (64-bit)
 Running under: Red Hat Enterprise Linux Server release 6.6 (Santiago)

And tidyverse::tidyverse_update() confirms that "All tidyverse
packages up-to-date"

Has anybody seen this before?

Thanks,
-steve

--
Steve Lianoglou
Computational Biologist
Cancer Immunology
Genentech

messages.subject: map_dbl() vs c() for processing POSIX datetime's
messages.subject_clean: map_dbl() vs c() for processing POSIX datetime's
messages.body_plain:
In the process of dynamically building a data.frame from an input text file I found that the map() and friends didn't work as I would have expected them to. c() does not strip off class attributes and map_dbl() does.

Specifically I was trying to create a data.frame with a column that was a POSIX datetime. If I use, for example, c(lubridate::now()) I get a double vector where each element has a class attribute that marks it as a POSIX datetime, just what I needed.

If instead I use something like map_dbl(1:3, function(x) {return(now())}) I get a double vector with the class attributes stripped from it, not what I expected. I have a work around that solves the problem but it complicates things. Is seems like map_dbl() should work the same way as c() and not strip off the class attribute.

Is there a reason that map_dbl() works differently than c()? Maybe I am missing something and there is an easier way to do what I am trying to do, but if map_dbl() worked the same as c() the code for what I want to do is pretty simple.

Below are a number of code snippets that illustrate the differences and what I am trying to do. I'm not sure that this is the right way to post a reprex.

Thanks,
Dan Sullivan

# Are map_dbl() and friends intentionally made to work
# differently than c()?
#
# The difference is that c() does not strip the class attribute
# from the scalars and map_dbl() does strip them. Note that
# c() is documented as stripping all attributes but in practice
# is does not strip the class attribute
#
# As is it is difficult to use map() to dynamically build
# data frames
# below are some examples of creating vectors and data.frames
# that contain doubles that are POSIX datetime's
library(tidyverse)
#> Loading tidyverse: ggplot2
#> Loading tidyverse: tibble
#> Loading tidyverse: tidyr
#> Loading tidyverse: readr
#> Loading tidyverse: purrr
#> Loading tidyverse: dplyr
#> Conflicts with tidy packages ----------------------------------------------
#> filter(): dplyr, stats
#> lag():    dplyr, stats
library(reprex)
library(lubridate)
#>
#> Attaching package: 'lubridate'
#> The following object is masked from 'package:base':
#>
#>     date
library(purrr)
#
# c() creates a double vector. It also copies the
# class attribute even though the documentation
# says it strips all attributes
datetimes1 <- c(now(), now(), now())
# so this shoes datetimes's
datetimes1
#> [1] "2017-08-18 13:31:04 EDT" "2017-08-18 13:31:04 EDT"
#> [3] "2017-08-18 13:31:04 EDT"
typeof(datetimes1)
#> [1] "double"
attributes(datetimes1[1])
#> $class
#> [1] "POSIXct" "POSIXt"
#
#
# map copies the class attribute but creates
# a list, not a character vector
datetimes2 <- map(1:3, function(x) {return (now())})
# This shows datetimes
datetimes2
#> [[1]]
#> [1] "2017-08-18 13:31:04 EDT"
#>
#> [[2]]
#> [1] "2017-08-18 13:31:04 EDT"
#>
#> [[3]]
#> [1] "2017-08-18 13:31:04 EDT"
# but it is a list not a double vector
typeof(datetimes2)
#> [1] "list"
attributes(datetimes2[[1]])
#> $class
#> [1] "POSIXct" "POSIXt"
#>
#> $tzone
#> [1] ""
#
#
# map_dbl creates a double vector but does
# not copy the class attribute
datetimes3 <- map_dbl(1:3, function(x) {return (now())})
# this shows doubles, not datetime's
datetimes3
#> [1] 1503077464 1503077464 1503077464
typeof(datetimes3)
#> [1] "double"
attributes(datetimes3[[1]])
#> NULL
#
# So map_dbl is inconsistent with how c() in fact works,
# but is consistent with how c() is documented
# However this creates a problem when map is used
# to, for example, create columns used to
# create a data.frame
#
# df1 includes the class attribute so the
# doubles are interpreted as datetime's
df1 <- data.frame(c(now(), now(), now()))
# this shows datetime's
df1
#>   c.now....now....now...
#> 1    2017-08-18 13:31:04
#> 2    2017-08-18 13:31:04
#> 3    2017-08-18 13:31:04
#
# df2 map is not useful because it produces
# a list that data.frame interprets as a data.frame row
df2 <- data.frame(map(1:3, function(x) { return (now())}))
# this shows a data.frame with a single row of datetimes
df2
#>   structure.1503077464.4804..class...c..POSIXct....POSIXt....tzone......
#> 1                                                    2017-08-18 13:31:04
#>   structure.1503077464.48044..class...c..POSIXct....POSIXt....tzone......
#> 1                                                     2017-08-18 13:31:04
#>   structure.1503077464.48048..class...c..POSIXct....POSIXt....tzone......
#> 1                                                     2017-08-18 13:31:04
#
# df3 map_dbl strips off all attributes so a datetime
# ends up being interpreted as just a double, not a datetime
df3 <- data.frame(map_dbl(1:3, function(x) { return (now())}))
# This shows a data.frame with 3 rows of doubles, not datetime's
df3
#>   map_dbl.1.3..function.x...
#> 1                 1503077464
#> 2                 1503077464
#> 3                 1503077464
#
# here is a work around, but is it very ugly to work with
# when both datatime's and scalar data needs to be processed
df4 <- data.frame(do.call("c",
    map(1:3, function(x) { return (now())})))
# This shows a data.frame with with 3 rows of datetime's
df4
#>   do.call..c...map.1.3..function.x...
#> 1                 2017-08-18 13:31:04
#> 2                 2017-08-18 13:31:04
#> 3                 2017-08-18 13:31:04

messages.body_plain:
Unlike c, map_dbl is type stable, which means that it always returns the same type of thing (in this case, a double). We don't have an elegant equivalent of map_dttm yet but you can always map() and then simplify some other way.

Hadley
